messages.content: You write the short explanations that first-year programming students in India type when a C quiz asks them "Why did you choose that answer?". Reply with a JSON object only.

A student was shown this C code and question.

Code:
int sum(int a[], int n) { if (n == 0) return 0; sum(a, n - 1); return a[n - 1]; }
// a = {1, 2, 3}

Question: What is sum(a, 3)?
The student answered: 6

The student holds this wrong belief and does not know it is wrong: The recursive call's result is combined automatically

Write 5 different explanations this student might type for why they chose that answer.
Voice: hesitant ("i think", "maybe", "not sure but"), one sentence of 8 to 18 words.

Rules:
- Each one must show the student's reasoning, not just repeat the answer.
- Write as the student, in the first person or with no subject. Do not judge the answer or say it is wrong.
- Do not name the idea as a rule and do not use textbook terms for the mistake.
- Make the 5 explanations differ in wording and in which part of the code they point at.

Return JSON: {"sentences": ["...", "..."]}

content: {"sentences": ["i think the recursive call adds its result to the final return so 1 plus 2 plus 3 makes 6.", "maybe the function keeps a running total each time it calls itself so the last value becomes 6.", "not sure but returning a[n-1] after the call probably adds that number to what came before.", "i think when n goes 3, 2, 1 the returns stack up together giving 1 plus 2 plus 3.", "maybe sum(a, n-1) brings back 3 and then return a[n-1] adds the current value into it."]}

sentences: i think the recursive call adds its result to the final return so 1 plus 2 plus 3 makes 6.
maybe the function keeps a running total each time it calls itself so the last value becomes 6.
not sure but returning a[n-1] after the call probably adds that number to what came before.
i think when n goes 3, 2, 1 the returns stack up together giving 1 plus 2 plus 3.
maybe sum(a, n-1) brings back 3 and then return a[n-1] adds the current value into it.
